--- title: "Africa: High Plateaus and Bright Cups" format: html: toc: true --- ## Narrative hook African coffees – especially from **Ethiopia** and **East Africa** – are often described as **bright, floral, and complex**, grown at **high elevations** on volcanic soils. In our dataset, Africa is a **smaller but distinctive** subset: > How do these African lots compare in **elevation**, **quality**, and **cup profile** to the rest of the world – and what can we safely say given the sample size? ## Who is represented ::: {#ec60f084 .cell execution_count=1} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ```{=html}
country n_samples
0 Ethiopia 11
1 Tanzania, United Republic Of 6
2 Uganda 3
3 Kenya 2
4 Madagascar 1
``` ::: ::: In this dataset: - There are **23 African lots** in total. - Most come from **Ethiopia** and **Tanzania**, with smaller contributions from **Uganda**, **Kenya**, and a single lot from **Madagascar**. This means: - Africa is **underrepresented** compared to the Americas and Asia-Pacific. - Country-level comparisons, especially for Kenya, Uganda, and Madagascar, should be read as **illustrative** rather than definitive. ## Elevation and quality Elevation is a core part of African origin stories. After cleaning and feet-to-metres conversion where needed: - African lots in this dataset are grown at **consistently high elevations** – roughly **1500–2360 metres**, with a median around **1750 m**. - Total cup scores range from about **82 to 86.5**, with a mean around **84.6**, firmly in the specialty range. ::: {#d2f49034 .cell execution_count=2} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` (count 23.000000 mean 1811.000000 std 226.958947 min 1500.000000 25% 1652.000000 50% 1750.000000 75% 1950.000000 max 2361.000000 Name: altitude, dtype: float64, count 23.000000 mean 84.626087 std 1.136777 min 82.170000 25% 83.915000 50% 84.500000 75% 85.330000 max 86.500000 Name: total_cup_points, dtype: float64) ``` ::: ::: ::: {#2279733f .cell execution_count=3} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ![](africa_files/figure-html/cell-4-output-1.png){} ::: ::: ::: {#86d4cdb3 .cell execution_count=4} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ![](africa_files/figure-html/cell-5-output-1.png){} ::: ::: With only 23 lots, the **altitude–score relationship** is noisy (correlation ≈ 0.2): there is **no strong trend** within this subset, although scores are generally high across the entire high-elevation range. ## Cup profile African coffees are often marketed as **bright, fruity, and aromatic**. Because our cupping data include full sensory scores, we can examine whether this subset aligns with that narrative. ::: {#8894d3b0 .cell execution_count=5} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=5} ```{=html}
country aroma flavor aftertaste acidity body balance sweetness
0 Ethiopia 7.86 7.87 7.76 8.02 7.82 7.77 10.0
1 Kenya 7.84 7.62 7.62 7.54 7.58 7.75 10.0
2 Madagascar 7.92 7.92 7.58 7.75 7.58 7.67 10.0
3 Tanzania, United Republic Of 7.90 7.81 7.75 7.86 7.85 7.78 10.0
4 Uganda 7.83 7.78 7.61 7.58 7.67 7.67 10.0
``` ::: ::: ::: {#b04448c1 .cell execution_count=6} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ![](africa_files/figure-html/cell-7-output-1.png){} ::: ::: In this sample: - All African origins show **high flavor and acidity scores**, consistent with the “bright and expressive” narrative. - Ethiopia and Tanzania (which have the most samples) sit slightly higher on average, but differences across countries are **small relative to overall high quality**. - Sweetness scores are uniformly high (close to the maximum), reflecting the dataset’s focus on well-prepared specialty lots. Because some countries have only a few lots, these patterns should be interpreted as **broad tendencies**, not precise national rankings. ## Regional takeaway Within this cupping dataset, Africa appears as: - A **high-elevation region**, with all sampled lots grown above roughly 1500 metres. - A cluster of **high-scoring specialty coffees**, with many lots in the top-specialty tier. - Sensory profiles that are **consistently bright and expressive**, especially in flavor and acidity, while remaining sweet and balanced. At the same time, Africa is **under-sampled** relative to its global importance in coffee production. The patterns we see here are best read as a **glimpse** of African specialty coffees rather than a comprehensive portrait. ## Future enhancements Planned extensions for this page include: - A **map of African origins**, highlighting which countries and sub-regions are represented in the dataset. - An **elevation+geography view** that links highland growing areas to the altitude distribution seen here. - Richer **flavor/aroma exploration**, such as interactive comparisons between Ethiopian and other East African profiles. These will be added later once the overall site structure and core narratives are fully in place.
